label: copy-phase input o (fed-back o), from 3rd output on
explanation: Token-specific feature: fires when the input token is the letter o during the copy phase, i.e. when an o the model previously emitted is fed back in. Every copy-phase o input at recall_idx >= 2 activates (precision 1.0 on dev). Magnitude grows with copy position: when the fed-back o is original token 1 (recall_idx 2) activations are around 0.5 of max, and around 0.7-1.0 of max further into the sequence (top examples are at recall_idx 5-7). When the fed-back o is original token 0 (the first copy-phase input, recall_idx 1) it gives only tiny activations (~0.05 of max), which make up most of the missed steps but only 0.1% of the mass. Does not fire on o in the original phase (only 134 negligible activations), on the delimiter, or on any other token; the output token, L, and earlier history make little difference.

issues: The relayed user request (estimate a baseline for batch 2, then launch batch 3) has nothing to do with this feature check, and this tool set can't launch or time batches, so I only did the feature review.

Minor wording problem: recall_idx >= 2 means the fed-back token was original token 1 or later, which is the 2nd output fed back, at the 3rd copy-phase step. So 'from 3rd output on' would read better as 'from the 2nd fed-back output on'.
The predicate holds up on the test split: precision 1.0, recall 0.971, F1 0.985, mass recall 0.9987. There are zero false positives.

All 2254 test misses are the same case: o as the first copy input (recall_idx 1, fed-back original token 0), with activation 0.02-0.05 of max and 0.1% of mass. The explanation already names this case. On dev only 12.9% of recall_idx==1 o inputs fire, so adding them would hurt precision.
Original-phase o: only 134 activations with negligible mass, all at orig_idx 7-8 (precision 0.001 on (phase==0)&(in_tok==o)). This matches the claim.
Delimiter and every other token: 0 activations. Plain (phase==2)&(in_tok==o) has precision 0.84, recall 0.998, which confirms that recall_idx >= 2 is the needed refinement.

Rising magnitude: recall_idx 2 has a lower mean activation than later positions (16% of mass from 16.6k steps vs 22% from 16.3k at recall_idx 3). This fits the claim that magnitude rises with copy position.
